name: Toulmin model
definition: Connect a claim to grounds through a warrant; add backing, a qualifier, and a rebuttal.
steps: Warrant: why those grounds support it
Rebuttal: when the claim may not apply

name: PREP
definition: Point, Reason, Example, Point: a compact framework for a clear spoken answer.

name: Steel-manning
definition: Restate the strongest reasonable version of an opposing position before responding.
steps: Check that the restatement is fair

name: Strategic concession
definition: Accept a valid limited point, then explain what it does and does not establish.

name: Ethos, pathos, logos
definition: Ethos concerns credibility, pathos the audience’s emotions, and logos the reasoning of the argument.
steps: Earn trust without substituting status for evidence
Connect the issue to human stakes

name: Four-step refutation
definition: Identify the claim, state the objection, support it, and explain the implication.
steps: They say: quote the actual claim fairly
I respond: name the specific flaw
Because: give a reason or counterexample

name: Purposeful pause
definition: Use silence at an idea boundary to help listeners process and to control your pace.
steps: Pause for one or two beats
Start the next sentence with intention

name: Cross-examination
definition: Use short, precise questions to clarify a claim, test its evidence, and expose unsupported assumptions.
steps: Test the scope with a counterexample
